adjuvant.name: alum
adjuvant.rationale: Aluminium-salt adjuvant: biases the response towards Th2 / IgG1 (README S10). Long clinical use makes it a defensible default for a first antibody-focused study; it is a weak inducer of IFN-gamma / Th1 responses, so it is a poor match for T-cell epitope readouts.

analysis_plan.analysis_population: All randomised animals with a valid sample at the primary timepoint, analysed in the arm allocated; numbers analysed per arm are reported
analysis_plan.below_lloq_rule: Values below the assay lower limit of quantification are assigned half the LLOQ, by one rule pre-specified for all arms
confirmatory_family: A03 (IgA-specific serine endopeptidase (tr|Q9K0B4|Q9K0B4_NEIMB, S7 final rank 1) 20 ug + alum) vs A06 (adjuvant only)
A04 (TonB-dependent receptor (NMB1829) (tr|Q9JXZ0|Q9JXZ0_NEIMB, S7 final rank 2) 20 ug + alum) vs A06 (adjuvant only)
A05 (Hemoglobin receptor (hmbR) (tr|Q9JYA8|Q9JYA8_NEIMB, S7 final rank 3) 20 ug + alum) vs A06 (adjuvant only)
exclusion_rules: Technical failure of dosing (documented leak or mis-injection), recorded before unblinding
Failed or insufficient sample at the primary timepoint (no imputation)
No exclusion of data points as 'outliers' after unblinding
exploratory_analyses: Dose-response, IgG subclass, kinetics and the falsification-map readouts: descriptive, with estimates and CIs, no confirmatory claims
Positive control vs naive: assay/model sensitivity check, outside the confirmatory family
analysis_plan.multiplicity_detail: Holm step-down across the 3 candidate-vs-adjuvant-only comparison(s), family-wise alpha 0.05 (two-sided); controls the family-wise error rate and is uniformly at least as powerful as Bonferroni. Sample size was planned at the Bonferroni level alpha/k = 0.01667.
analysis_plan.outlier_rule: No post-hoc outlier removal; any exclusion must be one of the pre-specified rules above
analysis_plan.primary_test: Welch two-sample t-test on log10 titres, each candidate arm (primary dose) vs adjuvant-only
sensitivity_analyses: Mann-Whitney U on the same comparisons with the same multiplicity correction (censored titres)
Cage as a cluster / random effect
Analysis including animals that reached a humane endpoint, where data exist

challenge_model.scope_note: No challenge phase is designed here. Challenge dose, route and any pathogen handling belong with the containment facility and its biosafety committee and are out of scope for this tool.
challenge_model.statement: Whether a susceptible small-animal challenge model exists for Neisseria meningitidis is UNKNOWN in the supplied pathogen context - CHECK the literature. No challenge model is established in this proposal and none is proposed or invented. The study measures immunogenicity only and cannot test protection in vivo.

correlate.statement: No correlate of protection is known or agreed for Neisseria meningitidis in the supplied pathogen context. Antibody titres from this study are therefore NOT evidence of protection. Most vaccines lack an agreed correlate (README S10); do not assume one - check, and read Plotkin (Clin Vaccine Immunol, 2010) before making correlate claims.

dosing.dose_ranging_note: All dose levels are run for the rank-1 candidate only; other candidates are run at the primary dose (Reduction). Dose-response is an exploratory, not confirmatory, comparison.
dosing.levels_status: ASSUMPTION - placeholder levels for the species; set from pilot data or literature
dosing.primary_dose_rationale: Highest dose level, so that a null result cannot be explained simply by under-dosing - the falsification claim ('no titre rise over adjuvant-only') is only informative at a dose given a fair chance. Reactogenicity at this level must be checked against the humane endpoints.

n=13 per group computed (noncentral t); the effect size is: ASSUMPTION - replace with pilot data.

Supplier, health status, body weight and housing conditions must be supplied; strain status: addressed.

Completed after the study; this tool produces no results.

The S8 in-vitro cascade cannot measure adaptive immunity, antibody titre, neutralisation, T-cell memory or protection, so a whole-animal study is the first experiment able to refute the S3/S5 predictions.

Group size is computed, not conventional (n=13 analysed per group, 3 comparison(s), holm correction); one shared adjuvant-only and naive arm serves all candidates; dose-ranging is top_ranked_only; padding only via the stated attrition allowance (0).
Explicit humane endpoints with monitoring frequency; bleed schedule minimised; welfare decisions never delayed for blinding.

honest_limits.evidence_ladder: predicted -> immunogenic in one species. A positive result does not move a candidate to 'works'.
honest_limits.source: README.md, section S10 'Honest limits' (README-sourced; not independently verified by this module)
statements: Mouse immunogenicity does not predict human protection. It shows an antigen is immunogenic in a mouse: necessary, not sufficient. (README S10)

Industry base rate for vaccines: Phase 1 to approval 39.6% (6.8% for non-industry sponsors). The narrowest transition is Phase 2 to 3 at 65.4% - precisely the step where immunogenicity data exists and efficacy data does not. No amount of preclinical work closes that gap. (README S10)
A positive animal result moves a candidate from 'predicted' to 'immunogenic in one species'. It does not move it to 'works'. (README S10)
This proposal reports no results of any kind and does not simulate assay readouts or clinical trials (README section 0).

humane_endpoints.anticipated_severity: mild (proposal only; AWERB / IACUC to confirm)

criteria.action: Humane killing (design default threshold; confirm against the licence/protocol severity limit)
Same-day consultation with the named animal-care / veterinary person; humane killing if not rapidly resolving
criteria.criterion: Persistent hunched posture, piloerection or markedly reduced activity

criteria.action: Veterinary consultation; humane killing if normal function is impaired
criteria.criterion: Injection-site ulceration, abscess or swelling impairing normal movement
Unable to reach food or water, or unresponsive to gentle stimulation
Excessive bleeding or failure to recover after blood sampling

monitoring.window: Day of each immunisation, after recovery and again at end of the working day
All remaining days of the schedule

humane_endpoints.note: Humane killing by a method approved for the project (UK: Schedule 1 / licence-specified; US: per the IACUC protocol and AVMA guidance). Animals reaching a humane endpoint are reported, not silently excluded.
humane_endpoints.weighing_frequency: On every immunisation and bleed day, and at least twice weekly otherwise

positive_control.note: CHECK: whether a licensed vaccine exists for this pathogen was not supplied, so no positive control arm is added. If one exists, add the licensed-vaccine positive control arm before ethics submission (README S10 minimum arms).

power_analysis.endpoint_scale: log10 antigen-specific serum IgG endpoint titre
notes: Sample size is PLANNED at the Bonferroni level alpha/k for either method; Holm's step-down procedure is uniformly at least as powerful, so the plan is conservative for Holm.

The adjuvant-only arm is shared by all k candidate comparisons, so the comparisons are positively correlated and Bonferroni is conservative; Dunnett's many-to-one test is a pre-specifiable alternative.
Group size is floored at 3 per group (variance estimation); floor applied: False.
Titres at or below the assay limit of detection violate the normality assumption; see the non-parametric sensitivity analysis in the analysis plan.
The result is only as good as the assumed effect size and SD. If the true effect is smaller, the study is under-powered (see sensitivity table).
power_analysis.test: Two-sided two-sample t-test (Welch in analysis; equal-n/equal-SD for planning), noncentral t

primary_endpoint.assay: Antigen-specific IgG ELISA with a pre-specified endpoint definition and lower limit of quantification
primary_endpoint.comparison: Each candidate + adjuvant arm at the primary dose vs the adjuvant-only arm (3 comparison(s))
primary_endpoint.definition: Log10 of the reciprocal endpoint dilution of serum IgG binding the immunising antigen, one value per animal, from the primary-timepoint bleed
primary_endpoint.lock_mechanism: Frozen, with the analysis plan, in the S11 pre-registration manifest (timestamped) and/or a public registry chosen by the investigators, before the first animal is dosed
primary_endpoint.name: Antigen-specific serum IgG endpoint titre (log10) at the primary timepoint
primary_endpoint.summary_measure: Difference in mean log10 titre (equivalently the geometric-mean titre ratio) with a 95% CI

randomisation.allocation_concealment: The allocation key is held by a named custodian (needs_human_input); other staff see only coded syringe and cage labels
randomisation.assay_plate_layout: Samples are coded and arms are interleaved and randomised across assay plates so that plate and batch effects are not confounded with arm
randomisation.cage_effects: Animals of one arm may need to be co-housed for welfare; cage is then recorded and used as a cluster in a sensitivity analysis
randomisation.method: Stratified randomisation to arms using a computer-generated sequence
randomisation.seed_recording: The random seed and generated allocation are recorded in the S11 pre-registration manifest
randomisation.sequence_generation: Seeded pseudo-random permutation, generated by someone who does not run the experiment
randomisation.unit_of_randomisation: individual animal (the experimental unit); cage ID is recorded for every animal

route.justification: Intramuscular: depot in muscle, the usual route for injectable and alum-adjuvanted vaccines. Targets the systemic compartment, which is what the primary endpoint (serum IgG) measures. Mouse muscle volume is small: injection volume per site must respect licence limits.

schedule.rationale: Prime-boost: immunise on days [0, 21, 42]; bleed on days [0, 20, 41, 56]. Bleeds on or before an immunisation day give baseline / pre-boost samples; the primary timepoint is day 56, 14 days after the final immunisation. Total bleed volume per animal must stay within the limits of the project licence / institutional guidance (needs_human_input).
terminal_procedures: Terminal exsanguination and serum collection at day 56.

design.scope_statement: This document is a study DESIGN. It specifies arms, group sizes, schedule, endpoints, statistics and ethics documentation. It contains no results, no simulated data and no assay values. It does not contain pathogen handling, culture or challenge-inoculum procedures: those belong with the containment facility and its biosafety committee and are deliberately out of scope for this tool.
secondary_endpoints: IgG titre at every scheduled bleed (kinetics) - exploratory.
IgG subclass profile (IgG1 vs IgG2a/c) at the primary timepoint - exploratory; reports the Th bias that the alum rationale (Th2) suggests.

species_selection.non_human_primates: Non-human primates are OUT OF SCOPE for this proposal (last resort; ethically and financially constrained, README S10). No NHP design is provided.
species_selection.rationale: Basic immunogenicity: cheap and fast (README S10). Wild-type mouse MHC (H-2) does NOT present the epitopes NetMHCpan predicted for human HLA, so the S5 T-cell and S6 population-coverage predictions are NOT under test in this design; only S3 (antibody titre), S5 B-cell epitopes and S7 (folded vs denatured) are.
species_selection.strain_rationale: BALB/c: Th2-leaning, IgG1-prone background with robust antibody responses - chosen as the default because the primary endpoint is a serum IgG titre. A poor choice if IFN-gamma / Th1 readouts are primary. IgG subclass detection must include IgG2a.

warnings: Licensed-vaccine availability not supplied: CHECK and add the positive control arm if one exists.
No established challenge model: the study can show immunogenicity only, not protection.
Effect size and SD are ASSUMPTIONS (no pilot data cited); the sample size is only as good as they are.
S3 LEAKAGE RISK (stream B's banner): the pretrained Vaxign-ML model was trained on all Protegen entries, so recovering known antigens is not validation
S4 screening was INCOMPLETE: gate(s) human_homology, allergenicity, toxicity, conservancy did not run, so these candidates were carried forward unscreened for them

S5 analyses that did not run: bcell_linear (unavailable: BepiPred-3.0 not configured (tools.bepipred3); BepiPred-2.0 is never used as a substitute); class_i (unavailable: no class I predictor available (backend=auto; netMHCpan not found, mhcflurry not installed)); class_ii (unavailable: netMHCIIpan not found (DTU licence; see docs/TOOLS_SETUP.md)); conformational (unavailable: DiscoTope-3.0 not configured (tools.discotope3)). The epitopes they would have produced do not exist

S6 population coverage did not run (could not obtain HLA frequencies: offline mode: refusing to fetch https://downloads.iedb.org/tools/population/LATEST/IEDB_Population_Coverage-3.0.2.tar.gz): there is no coverage data

S7 DEGRADED to sequence-only ranking (boltz not found on PATH (pip install boltz; MIT licence)): every structure field is empty and the final order rests on the S3, T-cell, B-cell and coverage terms that exist
